description: Extension methods for registering Tempo.Blazor services.

members.name: AddInMemoryNotifications
members.description: Replaces the default with so notifications are kept in memory. Also replaces with the same store so the badge count is live. Use this in demo / test applications where you want to see notifications without a real backend.

members.name: AddTempoBlazor
members.description: Registers the core Tempo.Blazor services shared by all component groups. ITmLocalizer: Singleton (stateless, thread-safe, backed by embedded JSON tables for en/cs/sk/fr) ITmRelativeTimeFormatter: Scoped relative-time formatter over a private TimeProvider that reads ITmUserTimeZone — the time comes from the host's TimeProvider (the system clock when none is registered), while the calendar day ("yesterday at 4:20 PM") is judged in the user's zone: the runtime's zone on WebAssembly, the browser's IANA zone on Blazor Server (UTC until the probe reports after the first interactive render, then the browser zone). The scoped ITmUserTimeZone instance is shared (the browser is read once per circuit); relative-time components re-render when the zone arrives and ITmUserTimeZone.SetZone lets a host profile setting win. Never replace the app-wide TimeProvider: Kestrel and cookie authentication are singletons that consume it, so a scoped replacement fails the host under ValidateScopes. No component takes a time-zone parameter for this. ThemeService: Scoped (per-circuit in Server mode, per-tab in WASM) ToastService: Scoped (per-circuit in Server mode, per-tab in WASM) DragDropService: Scoped drag/drop state shared by core components Add this call to your Blazor Program.cs: builder.Services.AddTempoBlazor(); To reword shipped translations in your application, register a decorator ITmLocalizer AFTER this call (it injects the built-in IStringLocalizer<TmResources> and overrides only the keys you list): builder.Services.AddTempoBlazor(); builder.Services.AddSingleton<ITmLocalizer, MyCustomTmLocalizer>(); To support e.g. Czech or Slovak localization, configure culture in Program.cs: var culture = new System.Globalization.CultureInfo("cs"); System.Globalization.CultureInfo.DefaultThreadCurrentCulture = culture; System.Globalization.CultureInfo.DefaultThreadCurrentUICulture = culture;
